subject: AzPC referral — unclaimed ledgers and field escalation paths
messages:
From: Carla Sanchez <carla.sanchez@contoso.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Azure Partner Center <pc-referrals@microsoft.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Contoso AZPC referral — orphaned accounts report

Markus / Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick help here. Partner Center flagged a batch of referrals tied to Contoso that are showing as "unclaimed" in the intake. Attached is the export we pulled (Contoso-unclaimed-accounts.csv) — ~120 rows, lots of SMBs and some mid-market accounts that look like duplicates of existing field-owned tenants.

Key ask: can Redwood confirm which of these should be routed to our field sellers vs. claimed by the Azure PC intake team? Contoso is pushing for a short list they want engaged before the quarter close.

CC'd the PC intake alias in case an automated reassign or retention window is needed. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

—Carla
Carla Sanchez
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Contoso
carla.sanchez@contoso.com

Attachment: Contoso-unclaimed-accounts.csv (csv, 120 rows)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Carla Sanchez <carla.sanchez@contoso.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso AZPC referral — orphaned accounts report

Thanks Carla — got the export. I pulled a quick sample and there are a few clear duplicates against accounts we already have field owners for (Tenant IDs match recent deals). I'll start an exceptions sheet and attach a working file (ownership_exceptions.xlsx) with my notes (duplicate, likely field claim, low-touch SMB).

Vanessa / Karthik — can you two take ownership of triage? Propose this workflow:
- Vanessa: run match vs. our account fabric and mark 'field-owner' for any tenant with an active seller or recent opportunity.
- Karthik: run policy on Partner Center claims for true unclaimed accounts and confirm whether we can auto-assign to an Azure seller or need to route to our sales enablement team.
- Laura: if there are contested accounts (two sellers/ambiguous), escalate into the 24-hour arbitration lane and I'll own outreach to Contoso.

Timebox: 48 hours for a triage list back to Carla. If we have >30 contested accounts we’ll propose a staged outreach (priority top 20).

I'll attach ownership_exceptions.xlsx for context.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachment: ownership_exceptions.xlsx (xlsx, 2 sheets: notes + candidates)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Carla Sanchez <carla.sanchez@contoso.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 12:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso AZPC referral — orphaned accounts report

Quick update after running a deterministic match + fuzzy name join against our account fabric. Findings (high level):
- 74 rows match existing Redwood accounts (I flagged seller owner in column 'owner_suggested').
- 33 look like pure new tenants with no match — candidate for PC auto-claim if policy allows.
- 13 are fuzzy / possible duplicates (ambiguous mapping across two sellers).

I've attached a triage CSV (unclaimed_accounts_triage.csv) with these columns: tenant_id, contoso_contact, match_status, owner_suggested, notes. For the ambiguous 13, I added a confidence score and last-touch timestamp.

Recommended next steps:
1) Karthik — can you confirm whether the 33 pure new tenants are eligible for immediate Azure PC seller assignment? If yes, ask PC to claim to nearest geo seller; if not, we need to run an enablement pass.
2) Laura / Markus — for the 13 ambiguous: propose we notify the two candidate sellers with a 48-hour claim window; no response -> we follow the arbitration lane (Markus to Contoso).

Happy to run a 30-minute triage call Monday if folks prefer.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment: unclaimed_accounts_triage.csv (csv, 120 rows)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, pc-referrals@microsoft.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso AZPC referral — unclaimed ledgers and field escalation paths

Putting in a short policy check with PC intake now. Summary of my ask to them:
- Confirm whether the 33 'new tenant' rows meet the criteria for immediate seller assignment (no active seller / no recent opportunity).
- If eligible, request claim to nearest Azure seller (US West / US Central) and return claim activity IDs.
- For ambiguous 13: request temporary hold + a two-business-day notification to candidate Redwood sellers before PC auto-claims.

PC responded (excerpt):
> "We can run an automated claim for unowned tenants provided there's no existing seller activity. For ambiguous mappings we can place a 48-hour hold and surface both candidate sellers for acceptance. After hold expires, claim will proceed to the nearest seller."

Plan: if PC confirms, we'll do the following this week:
- Day 0: PC place holds on ambiguous rows, claim new tenants to Azure sellers.
- Day 1: Vanessa notifies candidate Redwood sellers (email + Slack lane).
- Day 3: For any no-responders in ambiguous set, escalate to Markus + Laura for arbitration and prioritized outreach to Contoso.

I’ll paste PC claim IDs here once we get them. Marking this high priority for Contoso’s Q close.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
